subject: history
title: The Pacific War and the End of WWII
welcome_lead: From Pearl Harbor to Hiroshima, follow the war between Japan and the Allies that reshaped Asia and the world.
meta_desc: IBDP History Causes & Effects of Wars Adventure 3: causes, course and consequences of the Pacific War.
final_note: You have traced the war from Pearl Harbor to the surrender on USS Missouri. Decolonisation and the Cold War followed.

concepts.def: Japanese attack on the US Pacific Fleet at Hawaii on 7 December 1941.
Japanese imperial concept presenting conquest as Asian liberation from Western imperialism.
June 1942 US naval victory that turned the tide of the Pacific War.

walkthroughs.body_html: Japan's seizure of Manchuria (1931) and full-scale invasion of China (1937) brought it into confrontation with the United States. US embargoes, including the oil embargo of 1941, pressed Japan toward a strategic gamble: a knockout blow against US naval power to secure resources in Southeast Asia.

The surprise attack of 7 December 1941 brought the United States into the war. Initial Japanese conquests (Singapore, Philippines, Dutch East Indies) gave way after the carrier battles of Coral Sea and Midway (May-June 1942). Brutal campaigns in Guadalcanal, the Philippines, Iwo Jima and Okinawa pushed the front toward the Japanese home islands.

Conventional firebombing devastated Japanese cities; the atomic bombings of Hiroshima (6 August) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945) and the Soviet declaration of war on 8 August precipitated Emperor Hirohito's surrender broadcast on 15 August. Formal surrender followed aboard USS Missouri on 2 September 1945. The war catalysed decolonisation in Asia and shaped the emerging Cold War.
